newsitem.title: GREECE: Fraud charges laid over Greek pyramid schemes.
newsitem.headline: Fraud charges laid over Greek pyramid schemes.

text.p: A public prosecutor in the northern Greek city of Salonika charged a man with fraud on Wednesday over two collapsed get-rich-quick pyramid schemes, the state-run Athens News Agency said.
Thousands of northern Greeks are believed to have participated in the schemes, known as "Golden" and "Silver", whose estimated turnover was tens of millions of drachmas, the agency said.

Last week Albanians staged demonstrations in Tirana and other major cities blaming President Sali Berisha's government for the loss of their savings through the collapse of widespread pyramid investment schemes.

The Salonika prosecutor said 10,215 people had registered in one of the Greek schemes in November 1996 and turnover had reached 66 million drachmas ($257,500) but players who reached the top of the pyramid got no profits.

Salonika police chief Kostas Economou was quoted by the agency as saying he had asked the prosecutor not to charge as accomplices the thousands of people who put money in the the schemes because "it would create a social problem." ($1=256.3 Drachma)
